title: Internal ingress Terraform module: TLS offload, NLB passthrough, weighted backends and active health remediation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Deliver a production-ready Terraform module for Redwood Private that provides an internal ingress abstraction supporting both ALB TLS termination and NLB TLS passthrough, plus first-class support for weighted backend routing (for canaries/rollouts), robust health probes, and automated remediation hooks. The module should be reusable across customer VPCs, support terraform workspaces/versions, and include clear, low-risk upgrade paths for existing private deployments. Key requirements are: (1) ability to choose ALB or NLB per environment, (2) TLS termination options: ALB-terminate-with-ACM (recommended), NLB-tls-passthrough to targets, and optional ACM Private CA onboarding, (3) weighted target groups with lifecycle-managed target group attachments for canary traffic, (4) health check policies per backend with service-aware defaults and auto-remediation Lambda/SNS integrations, (5) internal DNS integration (route53 private zones) and IAM roles minimized to least privilege, (6) automated tests and example consumption module for on-prem and VPC AMI stacks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes 'provider' option set to 'alb' or 'nlb' and validates inputs
ALB mode creates internal ALB with HTTPS listener, ACM certificate attachment, target groups, and rule-based weighted routing between up to 5 backends
NLB mode supports TLS passthrough: listeners on 443 forwarding to target group TCP ports with option to attach non-ACM certs at target (for mTLS or customer-managed TLS)
Default health checks defined per target type (HTTP path /_health for HTTP targets, TCP probe for raw TCP targets) with configurable thresholds
Health probe auto-remediation: failing target group triggers SNS topic + Lambda that can deregister unhealthy targets and optionally scale ASG by +1 (configurable)
Module provides clear upgrade guide and backwards-compatible tfstate migration steps when switching listener types or swapping NLB <-> ALB
Example 'private-stack' tf config included in /examples demonstrating Route53 private zone records, KMS-encrypted secrets, and CI/CD integration
E2E tests: a small test harness shows traffic steering for a 10% canary using weighted backends and verifies health check behavior under simulated failure
migration_steps: Create a feature branch and add module usage in a non-prod workspace

If switching from NLB passthrough to ALB offload: provision ACM cert in private CA, add ALB listener and temporarily mirror traffic using weighted target groups (100% to old, 0% to new), then gradually shift weight
For state changes that replace resources (target groups/listeners): use terraform state mv to preserve attachments, and document explicit 'pre-apply' checklist in the module README
Provide a compatibility flag 'preserve_legacy_targets' to keep existing target registration behavior for one release cycle
Notify customers via release notes and provide a script for converting listener types (nlb->alb) with minimal downtime
notes: Opted to make ALB the default for HTTP workloads because we want native path/host routing and native TLS termination tied to ACM managed certs. NLB stays as an explicit opt-in for L4 passthrough and extremely low-latency TCP workloads.

We will not store private cert material in state; ACM + Private CA should be used for managed cert lifecycle. If customers require self-managed certs, document the manual process and mark as 'advanced'.
Module includes parameter 'internal_subnet_ids' and will set 'internal' scheme on LB resources. It will not create VPCs.
